column1: # splunk-precedence-allowlist.tsv — Splunk searches that mix OR and NOT in one paren
# scope, each reviewed once and signed off.
# WHY. pySigma's Splunk backend does not parenthesise a top-level OR against a top-level
# NOT, so `(a) OR (b) NOT (filter)` is correct only under the search command's documented
# precedence (parentheses, NOT, OR, AND). It is right today; it is one reading away from
# letting a branch escape its filter, and eval/where evaluate AND before OR. See #166.
# check-splunk-precedence.sh flags every such search and fails unless it has a row here,
# so the next one is a review conversation rather than a silent behaviour change. A row
# is NOT a suppression — it is a record that someone traced the binding and found it
# sound. The reason column is required and may not be '-'.
# FORMAT: <file><TAB><stanza title><TAB><reason>
# Keyed on stanza title because the generated conf carries no rule path. Retitling a rule
# drops it out of this list and fails the gate, which is the right direction to be wrong.
detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: Collected data staged into an archive (T1560.001)
column3: sigma condition is `(selection_password and 1 of add_verb_* and not filter_rar_no_password) or (((selection_staging_archiver and 1 of add_verb_*) or selection_staging_powershell) and not filter_backup_tooling)` (re-traced 2026-09-28 after the create-verb fix). The backend emits `(pw-image pw-flags (rar-add) OR (tar-create) OR makecab NOT -p-) OR ((archiver staging (verbs...)) OR (Compress-Archive) NOT backup-agent)`. Under search precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the first group is pw AND (any verb) AND NOT -p-, and the second is (archiver-with-verb OR Compress-Archive) AND NOT backup-agent - so the backup filter still gates only the staging half, which is the intent: the password branch is deliberately unfiltered by it (its only exclusion is its own `-p-` guard), and the two staging branches are both filtered.

column2: Mass file read - local data collection sweep (T1005)
column3: sigma condition is `(selection_list or selection_mask) and not filter_indexers`; the backend emits `source= (list) OR (mask) NOT (indexers)`. Under search precedence the leading source= term AND the filter both bind to both branches, which is the intent. Long-form note lives in the rule's own description (#165)

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: Data encrypted for impact - BitLocker driven from the command line
column3: sigma condition is `1 of selection_* and not filter_provisioning`; the backend emits `(manage-bde) OR (powershell cmdlet) NOT ParentImage=*\\TSManager.exe`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own term first and the juxtaposed implicit AND binds loosest, so it reads ((manage-bde) OR (cmdlet)) AND NOT TSManager - the imaging filter covers BOTH branches, which is the intent: a task sequence drives manage-bde and Enable-BitLocker alike, so neither branch should alert on it. Same shape and same reading as the archive-staging row above. Added with the filter in #261

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: AWS snapshot/AMI shared outside the organisation (T1537)
column3: sigma condition is `selection_grant and (selection_public or (selection_named and not filter_own_accounts))`; the backend emits `eventSource= eventName= (public x3) OR (named x3 NOT (own-accounts x3))`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the inner paren reads (named1 OR named2 OR named3) AND NOT (own-accounts), so the allowlist covers all three named branches; the outer OR group then binds under the two juxtaposed IN terms, so eventSource and eventName gate every branch. The three public branches sitting OUTSIDE that paren is the INTENT, not a miss - a `group: all` share is public and no account allowlist can make it benign, which is the whole two-tier design (#262). Same shape and reading as the archive-staging and BitLocker rows above

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column3: sigma condition is `1 of selection_* and not filter_iac`; the backend emits `(setMetadata + added_metadata_keys) OR (setMetadata + modified_metadata_keys) NOT principal_email=iac`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own term first and the juxtaposed implicit AND binds loosest, so it reads ((added) OR (modified)) AND NOT iac - the IaC allowlist covers BOTH arms, which is the intent: a provisioning principal writing a startup script is benign whether the key is new on the instance or overwrites an existing one, so exempting only one arm would leave the other alerting on every image build. Same shape and same reading as the BitLocker and archive-staging rows above. Added with the rule in #305

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: Mass service stop - the ransomware pre-encryption teardown (T1489)
column3: sigma condition (base rule service_stop_command) is `1 of selection_* and not filter_maintenance_parent`; the backend emits `(net stop) OR (sc stop/disable) OR (taskkill /f) OR (Stop-Service/Stop-Process) NOT ParentImage=maintenance` as the leading search command, ahead of `| bin | stats dc(CommandLine)`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own term first and the juxtaposed implicit AND binds loosest, so it reads (net OR sc OR taskkill OR powershell) AND NOT maintenance - the allowlist covers all four arms before the count, which is the intent: a suite's restart tooling mixes net, sc and PowerShell stops, and exempting only one arm would leave the others counting toward the burst. Same shape and same reading as the BitLocker row above. Added with the filter in #324

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: Registry Run key pointing at a user-writable path or an interpreter (Sysmon 13)
column3: sigma condition is `run_key and 1 of target_* and not filter_user_apps`; the backend emits `TargetObject IN (run keys) Details IN (user-writable) OR Details IN (interpreters) NOT Details=(allowlisted app)` with no parens. Under search precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) NOT binds first, OR joins the two target lists, and the implicit AND ties both to the run-key list and to the filter - so the allowlist applies to both branches, which is the intent.

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: LSASS process access with dump-shaped rights
column3: sigma condition is `selection and selection_access and not filter_av`; the backend emits `TargetImage=lsass (suffix IN) OR (prefix IN) NOT (agent allowlist)`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own paren first and the OR groups the two GrantedAccess lists, so it reads lsass AND (VM_READ-suffix OR full-rights-prefix) AND NOT agents - the EDR allowlist covers BOTH access branches, which is the intent. Traced 2026-09-28 when the exact-mask list became a VM_READ-bit match

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: HashiCorp Vault auth role / AppRole / auth method created (persistence)
column3: sigma condition is `selection and 1 of paths_* and not filter_secret_id_admin and not (secret_id_mint and filter_ci_orchestrator)`; the backend emits `type op (identity paths IN) OR request.path=sys/auth/* NOT (secret-id admin paths) NOT (mint paths entity=orchestrator)`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the OR groups only the two path branches and each NOT is its own term, so it reads request AND create|update AND (identity paths OR sys/auth) AND NOT secret-id admin AND NOT (mint AND orchestrator) - both exemptions bind to every path branch, which is the intent. Re-traced 2026-09-29 when the secret-id lookup/destroy exclusion was added

column1: detections/siem/splunk/savedsearches.generated.conf
column2: WMI event subscription persistence - command-line or script consumer
column3: sigma condition is `created and (selection_commandline_payload or selection_script_consumer or selection_commandline_any) and not filter_known_consumers`; the backend emits `Operation=Created (keyword arm) OR (script arm) OR (command-line arm) NOT Destination=allowlist`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own term and the OR groups the three parenthesised arms, so it reads Created AND (keyword OR script OR command-line) AND NOT allowlist - the Destination allowlist covers all three arms and Created gates them all, which is the intent. Traced 2026-09-29 when the allowlist was widened from one arm to all
